summary: The frozen array printing candidate is refuted: arrays accepted by parsing remain within the printer’s nesting limit. Coverage is limited to this focused candidate.

assessment.necessity_reason: The harness prints only the tree returned by cJSON_ParseWithOpts. Parsing creates arrays through parse_array and rejects array or object nesting at the same pre-increment threshold used by the new printer.

before.requirement: Print a parser-produced array at every nesting depth accepted by parsing, without failing solely because of its depth.
before.reason: The old array printer has no depth rejection, and the harness passes the parsed tree directly to a print function.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: The complete parse dispatch sends array and object input to their respective parsers.
Array parsing rejects nesting at the limit before incrementing depth.
Object parsing applies the same threshold to mixed nesting.

after.requirement: Print a parser-produced array at every nesting depth accepted by parsing, without failing solely because of its depth.
after.reason: Both print paths start at depth zero. The new array guard rejects only a depth that the parser’s array and object guards already reject.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: The complete parse dispatch creates arrays through parse_array and sends mixed nesting through parse_object.
Array parsing uses the printer’s pre-increment nesting threshold.
Object parsing applies the same threshold to mixed nesting.
Unbuffered printing starts with depth zero.
Buffered printing also starts with depth zero.

assessment.comparison_reason: The same old harness prints a parser-returned tree on both sides. The new array depth check does not exclude any parser-accepted array depth.
